Applies to All Sankalpa employees unless a written employment

agreement states otherwise

How to use this handbook
This handbook explains common employment policies, expected workplace behavior, approval paths and operating 
procedures. Where a written employment agreement, benefits plan document or local statutory requirement is more 
specific, the more specific document controls.
 Managers are responsible for applying policies consistently and escalating unclear cases to People Operations.

 Employees should ask before acting when a policy is unclear, especially for travel, security, conflicts of interest or external 
communication.
 Nothing in this fictional handbook creates a contract of employment or guarantees continued employment, compensation, 
benefits or a particular work arrangement.
 Policy exceptions must be documented in writing by the authorized approver identified in the relevant section.
RAG testing tip

RAG testing tip
Policy IDs, defined terms, approval requirements, time limits and exception paths are intentionally explicit so retrieval 
systems can be tested on precise questions and edge cases.

1. Welcome and Company Principles
Policy at a glance
Purpose Set expectations for how employees work together and how this 
handbook should be interpreted.
Applies to All employees.
Policy owner People Operations.
Sankalpa is a fictional technology and operations company used in this handbook simulation. The company expects

employees to deliver reliable work, protect customers and company information, raise concerns early and treat 
colleagues with professionalism.
Core working principles
 Customer trust: make decisions that protect users, customers and confidential information.
 Ownership: follow through on commitments, surface blockers early and document important decisions.
 Respect: challenge ideas without attacking people, and avoid harassment, discrimination or retaliation.

 Security by default: use approved systems, least-privilege access and secure handling practices.
 Learn and improve: seek feedback, share knowledge and correct mistakes transparently.
Manager responsibilities
 Explain team expectations and any role-specific procedures.
 Review leave, remote work, travel and expense requests within a reasonable time.
 Escalate potential safety, conduct, legal or security issues rather than handling serious matters informally.
 Avoid retaliation against employees who raise concerns in good faith.

2. Employment Framework
Policy at a glance
Employment categories Regular full-time, regular part-time, fixed-term, intern/trainee, 
and approved contractor classifications.
Probation May apply if stated in the employment letter.
Personnel records Employees must keep contact, emergency and payment 
information current.
Employment records

information current.
Employment records
 Employees must promptly update their personal contact details, emergency contact, bank/payment information and 
required identity or tax documentation through the HR system.
 Access to personnel files is limited to authorized business purposes.
 Changes to title, compensation, reporting line or employment status require documented approval before taking effect.
Role changes and transfers

Role changes and transfers
Internal transfers may be considered based on role eligibility, performance, business need and manager release 
timing. Employees should not assume a transfer is final until they receive written confirmation from People Operations.
Important distinction
A verbal discussion about a promotion, transfer, salary change or conversion does not by itself change an employee's 
employment terms. Written confirmation is required.

3. Working Hours, Timekeeping and Attendance
Policy at a glance
Standard hours 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday.
Flexibility Employees may request flexible arrangements from their 
manager.
Unplanned absence Notify the manager before the workday begins, unless an 
emergency makes that impossible.

emergency makes that impossible.
Attendance records Employees must accurately record time or attendance when 
their role requires it.
3.1 Standard schedule
Sankalpa standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday. Team schedules may vary for 
customer coverage, shifts, releases or business continuity. Managers must communicate recurring schedule changes 
in advance where practical.
3.2 Flexible schedules

3.2 Flexible schedules
 Employees may request a different start/end time when business coverage is maintained.
 Flexible schedules are not automatic and may be changed or withdrawn when business needs change.
 Employees must remain reachable during agreed collaboration hours and attend required meetings.
3.3 Attendance and lateness
 If an employee expects to be late or absent unexpectedly, they should notify their manager before the workday begins.

 Repeated unexplained lateness, unreported absence or inaccurate time records may lead to corrective action.
 In an emergency, notification may be made as soon as reasonably possible by the employee or an appropriate contact.
Example
An employee whose commute is disrupted may ask to start remotely and arrive later. The manager can approve the 
arrangement if coverage and role requirements are met.

4. Hybrid and Remote Work
Policy at a glance
Eligibility Hybrid work is available to eligible roles with manager approval.
Availability Remote employees must remain available during agreed 
working hours.
Security Company information must be protected regardless of work 
location.
Default simulation guideline Eligible teams may normally approve up to 2 remote days per

week unless a team policy states otherwise.
4.1 Approval and eligibility
Hybrid work is a work arrangement, not a permanent entitlement. Eligibility depends on the role, performance, security 
requirements, customer obligations and team coverage. Managers may require office attendance for onboarding, 
planning, customer work, training, incidents or other business needs.
4.2 Remote workspace requirements

4.2 Remote workspace requirements
 Use a reasonably private workspace and prevent unauthorized people from viewing or hearing confidential information.
 Use company-managed devices and approved networks, VPNs and applications when required.
 Do not print sensitive information at home unless specifically authorized and a secure disposal method is available.
 Report lost devices, suspected phishing, credential compromise or data exposure to IT immediately.
4.3 Temporary remote work

4.3 Temporary remote work
A short-term remote request due to travel disruption, minor illness, home maintenance or similar circumstances may 
be approved by the manager. Remote work is not automatically a substitute for sick leave when the employee is 
unable to work.
Cross-border work
Working from another country or jurisdiction requires advance approval from People Operations, Security and the relevant
business leader because payroll, tax, immigration, data access and customer restrictions may apply.

5. Leave and Time Off
Policy at a glance
Annual leave 12 days per calendar year.
Sick leave 6 days per calendar year.
Planned leave Request through the HR system and obtain manager approval 
before making non-refundable commitments.
Unplanned absence Report to the manager before the workday begins when

reasonably possible.
Leave type Simulation entitlement Approval / notice
Annual leave 12 days / calendar year Manager approval; request in advance.
Sick leave 6 days / calendar year Notify manager promptly; documentation 
may be requested for extended absence.
Bereavement Up to 3 working days Notify manager; People Operations can 
approve exceptions.
Marriage / personal event Up to 2 working days Manager approval; request in advance.

Parental / statutory leave As applicable under the governing plan or 
law
Coordinate with People Operations.
Unpaid leave Case-by-case People Operations + manager approval.
5.1 Annual leave
 Annual leave should be planned to avoid critical delivery periods where reasonable.
 Managers should consider fairness, staffing, previously approved leave and operational commitments.

 For this simulation, up to 5 unused annual-leave days may carry forward into the next calendar year and should normally 
be used by 31 March. Any different rule in a benefits or local policy document controls.
5.2 Sick leave
 Sick leave is for an employee who is unwell or needs qualifying medical care.
 Employees should not work merely to avoid using sick leave if they are not fit to perform their duties safely.

 People Operations may request reasonable documentation for extended or repeated absence, subject to applicable rules.
Leave is not remote work
If an employee is too unwell to work, the appropriate status is sick leave rather than “working from home.” A manager may 
approve remote work only when the employee is actually able to work.

6. Compensation, Payroll and Overtime
Policy at a glance
Pay cycle Monthly, on the last working day of the month for this 
simulation.
Payroll corrections Report suspected errors to payroll within 10 working days of the 
pay statement.
Overtime Must be approved in advance when the role/policy requires paid 
overtime.
6.1 Salary and payroll

overtime.
6.1 Salary and payroll
 Base salary and any fixed allowances are stated in the employee's written compensation documents.
 Applicable deductions may be made for taxes, benefits or other lawful and authorized purposes.
 Employees should review pay statements promptly and report suspected errors to payroll@sankalpa.example.
6.2 Overtime and additional hours
Employees should not assume that working additional hours creates an entitlement to overtime pay or compensatory

time. Eligibility depends on role classification and applicable rules. Where prior approval is required, employees must 
obtain it before working additional scheduled hours except during genuine emergencies.
6.3 Compensation reviews
Compensation may be reviewed periodically based on market data, role scope, performance, internal equity and 
business conditions. A performance review does not guarantee a salary increase, bonus or promotion.

7. Benefits and Wellness
Policy at a glance
Core benefits Health insurance and an annual wellness allowance for eligible 
employees.
Eligibility Defined by the applicable benefit plan and employment 
category.
Questions People Operations can explain eligibility, enrollment and claim 
processes.
7.1 Health insurance

processes.
7.1 Health insurance
Sankalpa provides health insurance to eligible employees under the terms of the applicable plan. Coverage levels, 
dependent eligibility, exclusions, waiting periods and claims procedures are governed by the plan documents. If this 
handbook conflicts with a plan document, the plan document controls.
7.2 Wellness allowance
 For this simulation, eligible employees may claim up to INR 12,000 per calendar year for approved wellness expenses.

 Examples may include fitness membership, preventive health checks, ergonomic accessories or approved mental-
wellbeing services.
 Claims require a valid receipt and must be submitted within 30 days of purchase and before the annual cutoff 
communicated by People Operations.
 Cash, gift cards, alcohol, tobacco, gambling, personal electronics and non-wellness lifestyle purchases are not 
reimbursable under this allowance.
Plan documents control

Plan documents control
Benefits are one of the areas where a handbook should not be treated as the only source. Eligibility, exclusions and claims 
are governed by the current plan terms.

8. Performance, Feedback and Development
Policy at a glance
Review cadence Formal performance reviews twice each year.
Feedback Employees and managers should exchange ongoing feedback 
between formal reviews.
Development Training and development support may be approved based on 
role relevance and budget.
8.1 Performance reviews

8.1 Performance reviews
Sankalpa conducts performance reviews twice each year. Reviews may consider goal delivery, role expectations, 
quality, collaboration, customer impact, security/compliance behavior and demonstration of company principles.
8.2 Performance improvement
When performance is below expectations, the manager should clarify the gap, expected standard, support available

and review timeline. Depending on severity and circumstances, Sankalpa may use coaching, written expectations, a 
formal improvement plan or other corrective action.
8.3 Learning support
 Role-relevant courses, certifications or conferences may be approved when there is a clear business benefit.
 Approval should be obtained before booking or purchasing.
 Reimbursement may be subject to budget limits, completion evidence and any written learning agreement.

9. Workplace Conduct and Respect
Policy at a glance
Standard Treat colleagues, customers, vendors and visitors respectfully.
Prohibited behavior Harassment, discrimination, bullying, threats, retaliation, 
deliberate sabotage and serious dishonesty.
Reporting Raise concerns with a manager, People Operations or the 
ethics channel.
9.1 Professional conduct

ethics channel.
9.1 Professional conduct
 Communicate respectfully, including in chat, email, meetings and code/document reviews.
 Do not engage in insulting, humiliating, discriminatory or sexually inappropriate conduct.
 Do not retaliate against a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation.
 Do not intentionally damage company property, systems, records or another person's work.
9.2 Alcohol, drugs and impairment

9.2 Alcohol, drugs and impairment
Employees must not perform work while impaired in a way that creates a safety, security or performance risk. At 
company events where alcohol is legally permitted, employees remain responsible for professional behavior and safe 
transportation.
9.3 Workplace relationships
Employees should disclose a close personal or romantic relationship when one person directly or indirectly influences

the other person's pay, performance rating, promotion, scheduling or employment decision. The company may adjust 
reporting lines or decision rights to manage the conflict.

10. Grievances, Reporting and Non-Retaliation
Policy at a glance
Channels Manager, People Operations, ethics@sankalpa.example, or 
Security/IT for security incidents.
Confidentiality Information is shared on a need-to-know basis; absolute 
confidentiality cannot be guaranteed.
Non-retaliation Retaliation for good-faith reporting or participation in an

investigation is prohibited.
10.1 Raising a concern
1.  Use the channel that feels appropriate for the issue. Employees do not have to report to a manager who is involved in the 
concern.
2.  Provide facts, dates, people involved and relevant documents when available. Avoid altering evidence.
3.  People Operations or another authorized team will assess the concern and determine the appropriate review process.

4.  The company will share outcomes to the extent appropriate, while respecting privacy and legal constraints.
10.2 Urgent concerns
 Immediate safety threat: contact local emergency services first, then company security or management.
 Suspected phishing, credential theft, device loss or data exposure: contact IT/Security immediately.
 Potential fraud, bribery, harassment or retaliation: contact People Operations or the ethics channel promptly.
Good-faith reporting

Good-faith reporting
A report does not need to be proven correct to be protected as a good-faith report. Knowingly false or malicious 
allegations, however, may themselves violate policy.

11. Information Security and Acceptable Use
Policy at a glance
Passwords Use strong, unique passwords and approved multi-factor 
authentication.
Devices Protect company devices and do not disable security controls.
Incidents Report suspected phishing, credential compromise, malware, 
device loss or data loss immediately.

device loss or data loss immediately.
Software Use approved software and services for company data.
11.1 Account security
 Never share passwords, authentication codes, API keys or recovery codes with another person.
 Use the company password manager where provided and enable MFA on supported business systems.
 Lock screens when away from a device and prevent shoulder-surfing in public spaces.
11.2 Acceptable use

11.2 Acceptable use
 Company systems are primarily for legitimate business use. Limited personal use may be permitted if lawful, low-risk and 
does not interfere with work.
 Do not install unauthorized software, bypass security tools, use company systems for illegal activity, or store company 
data in unapproved personal accounts.
 Do not upload confidential company or customer data into public AI tools, code assistants, file-sharing sites or consumer

cloud services unless the service is approved for that data classification.
11.3 Incident reporting
Employees must report suspected phishing or data loss to IT immediately. Fast reporting is expected even when the 
employee is unsure whether an incident actually occurred. Employees should preserve evidence and avoid deleting 
suspicious messages or files unless Security instructs them to do so.
Security contact

Security contact
For this simulation: security@sankalpa.example and ithelp@sankalpa.example. Lost device or suspected account 
takeover should be treated as urgent.

Employees should collect, access, copy, export and retain only the information needed for the approved business 
purpose. Convenience alone is not a reason to create personal copies of sensitive data.
12.2 Sending information

12.2 Sending information

 Use approved secure transfer tools for large or sensitive files.
 Do not forward company email to personal accounts for convenience.

13. Company Devices and Asset Management
Policy at a glance
Ownership Company-issued devices and accessories remain company 
property unless transferred in writing.
Care Employees must take reasonable care of devices and report 
damage or loss promptly.
Return All company property must be returned by the final working day 
unless otherwise instructed.

unless otherwise instructed.
13.1 Device use
 Keep operating systems, endpoint security and required applications updated.
 Do not lend company devices to family members or other unauthorized people.
 Use approved encryption and screen-lock settings.
 Do not attempt hardware repairs or security modifications unless authorized by IT.
13.2 Lost or stolen devices
1.  Notify IT/Security immediately.
2.  Provide the device type, asset tag if known, last known location and time of loss.

3.  Change credentials or follow containment instructions if requested.
4.  File a police or venue report if instructed or appropriate.
Do not wait for certainty
If a device containing company data might be lost, report it immediately. Security can close the incident later if the device 
is found.

14. Travel and Expense Reimbursement
Policy at a glance
Travel approval Written manager approval is required before booking business 
travel.
Expense standard Reasonable, necessary business expenses are reimbursable 
when properly documented.
Receipt deadline Submit receipts through the expense portal within 30 days.

Exceptions Finance approval is required for policy exceptions or missing-
document cases.
Expense Default simulation rule Notes
Air travel Economy class for standard trips Premium class requires documented exception 
approval.
Hotel Reasonable market rate near business location Use preferred suppliers where available.
Meals Actual reasonable cost within local guideline Personal alcohol is not reimbursable unless 
part of an approved client event.

part of an approved client event.
Ground transport Taxi/rideshare/public transport or mileage 
where approved
Choose safe, practical, cost-conscious options.
Internet / business calls Reasonable business use while travelling Receipt or itemized record required where

14.1 Before booking
 Obtain written manager approval describing the business purpose and approximate dates/cost.
 Use the approved booking channel when one is available.

 Do not select a materially more expensive option for personal convenience unless the employee pays the difference and 
the arrangement is approved.
14.2 Submitting expenses
1.  Submit the expense in the portal within 30 days of the transaction or trip completion.
2.  Attach an itemized receipt where available and state the business purpose.
3.  Identify attendees for business meals or client entertainment when required.
4.  Return any unused company advance or resolve rejected items promptly.

Example
A hotel receipt submitted 45 days after travel is outside the normal 30-day deadline. The employee should still submit it, 
explain the delay and obtain any required Finance exception approval rather than altering the date or omitting the 
expense.

16. Conflicts of Interest, Gifts and Anti-Bribery
Policy at a glance
Conflict rule Disclose actual or potential conflicts before participating in the 
decision.
Bribery Offering, requesting or accepting bribes or kickbacks is 
prohibited.
Gifts Must be modest, infrequent, lawful and not intended to 
influence a business decision.
16.1 Common conflicts

16.1 Common conflicts
 Selecting or managing a vendor owned by a close relative or someone with whom the employee has a significant personal 
relationship.
 Using confidential company information for personal investment or outside business advantage.
 Holding outside employment that interferes with Sankalpa duties or creates a competitive/confidentiality conflict.
 Hiring, evaluating or approving compensation for a person where there is a close personal relationship that could impair

objectivity.
16.2 Gifts and hospitality
For this simulation, gifts with a value above INR 5,000 from a current or prospective vendor, customer or partner 
require written Ethics approval before acceptance. Cash or cash-equivalent gifts should not be accepted regardless of 
value. Lower-value gifts can still be inappropriate if they are frequent or connected to a pending decision.
Never split a gift or expense

Never split a gift or expense
Breaking one gift or expense into smaller amounts to stay below an approval threshold defeats the control and violates 
policy intent.

18. Intellectual Property and Company Records
Policy at a glance
Work product Rights in work created within the scope of employment are 
governed by the employee agreement and applicable law.
Open source Use must comply with approved licensing and security 
processes.
Records Business records must be accurate and retained or deleted

according to approved schedules and legal holds.
18.1 Intellectual property
Employees should promptly disclose inventions, designs, code, models, documentation or other work product when 
required by their employment agreement or company process. Employees must not incorporate third-party material 
without permission or a compatible license.
18.2 Open-source software
 Review license obligations before using or distributing open-source components.

 Do not copy code from unknown sources into company products without review.
 Follow Security and Engineering procedures for dependency scanning and vulnerability management.
18.3 Records integrity
Employees must not falsify expenses, time records, customer records, test results, approvals or other business 
records. If a legal hold or investigation notice is issued, relevant records must not be deleted or altered until the hold is 
released.

19. Corrective Action and Investigations
Policy at a glance
Approach Response depends on severity, facts, prior history, intent and 
risk.
Possible actions Coaching, warning, improvement plan, access restriction, 
suspension, reassignment or separation.
Investigations Employees are expected to cooperate honestly and preserve 
relevant information.

relevant information.
19.1 Corrective action
Sankalpa may use progressive corrective action where appropriate, but the company is not required to use every step 
in every case. Serious misconduct, security violations, fraud, violence, harassment, retaliation or deliberate falsification 
may justify accelerated action depending on the facts.
19.2 Investigation expectations
 Provide truthful information and relevant documents.
 Do not destroy, alter or conceal evidence.

 Do not destroy, alter or conceal evidence.
 Do not retaliate against participants or attempt to coordinate false accounts.
 Respect confidentiality instructions intended to protect the process, while recognizing employees may have rights that 
cannot be waived by policy.
No automatic outcome
A complaint, investigation or allegation does not by itself establish misconduct. Decisions should be based on the 
available evidence and applicable standards.

20.1 Resignation
Employees who resign from Sankalpa are expected to provide 30 days of written notice. People Operations will

Confidentiality, intellectual-property, non-solicitation or other post-employment obligations continue to the extent stated 
in the applicable agreement and law. Former employees must not retain company or customer data.

A2. Employee Scenarios and FAQs
Scenario 1 - Sick but able to work from home?
If the employee is well enough to work and the role is eligible, the manager may approve temporary remote work. If the 
employee is not fit to work, sick leave should be used. Remote work is not a substitute for medical recovery.
Scenario 2 - Forgotten travel receipt

Scenario 2 - Forgotten travel receipt
Submit the claim within 30 days if possible. If the receipt is missing, provide alternative documentation and an 
explanation. Finance decides whether the expense can be reimbursed; the employee must not create or alter a receipt.
Scenario 3 - Suspicious email from the CEO
Do not rely on the sender name alone. Do not click links or send credentials. Report the message through the security

channel immediately, especially if it asks for password resets, gift cards, payments or confidential files.
Scenario 4 - Vendor sends an expensive gift
If the value is above INR 5,000, written Ethics approval is required before acceptance. Cash or cash equivalents 
should not be accepted regardless of value. When in doubt, disclose and ask before accepting.
Scenario 5 - Working from another country for two weeks

Manager approval alone is not enough. Cross-border work requires advance review by People Operations, Security 
and the relevant business leader because immigration, tax, payroll, customer and data-location restrictions may apply.
Scenario 6 - Performance review is strong. Is a raise guaranteed?
No. Performance reviews and compensation decisions are related but separate. Compensation also depends on role 
scope, market data, internal equity and business conditions.
